Wakupati Narayan Temple is a two-story pagoda temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu that was built in 1667 AD and is surrounded by a stone-paved courtyard. The ornate, golden mandir survived the 2015 earthquake despite some damage to neighboring buildings; note the entourage of five Garudas supported on pillars on the backs of turtles.courtyard. This is the only location where four Garudas can be seen.
Narayan temple with all 10 avatar.

Wakupati Narayan Temple is a two-story pagoda temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu, enclosed within a stone-paved courtyard. It is located at Suryamadhi, Bhaktapur. A few minutes of walk from Chyamasingha towards the west leads you to this temple.

This temple is also called Wakupati Changu Narayan temple. People who couldn’t go to Changunarayan for prayer choose to go to Wakupati Narayan temple. It is like a substitution of the Changu Narayan temple.

About the erection of this temple, it is said that the temple was built in 1667. However, there is one interesting story regarding the emergence of the Wakupati Narayan, the deity. As per the story, one devotee of Narayan who daily went to Changu Narayan had to stop going there because of the harvesting works.

He was too busy to visit the temple thus he remembers the Narayan, pray spiritually and go to work. One evening when he was returning back home with the sack of paddy, he found the image of Lord Vishnu in his sack. Since it was found within the sack of paddy, it was named Wakupati Narayan.

Here, Wakupati Narayan simply means the seen Vishnu while carrying the sack of paddy.

The temple by date seems more archaic than the Nyatapola temple and is in very good shape today. Despite some damage to neighbouring buildings, the ornate, golden temple survived the 2015 quake outlasting various distinct quakes.

Well, while you visit this temple, you would surely note the entourage of five Garudas supported on pillars on the backs of turtles. This is the only place where one would see five Garudas standing back to back in a row. However, the nearest one seems like a devotee rather than the Garuda as in the Dattatraya temple. You can clearly recognize the human face in it. But there are wings too to call him human as well.

Along with such mysterious creatures, there is an ancient stone tap inside the courtyard. Also, the stone scriptures of God and Goddesses. There is a statue of Lord Ganesha on the right side of the temple. Similarly, there is the image of Dasavatar of Lord Vishnu right behind the temple. You can have a guess recognising each of them while existing from that narrow space of the temple.

Nearby, there is a stone image of Goddess Saraswoti. There is even a temple of Chinna Masta, one among the Das Mahavidhyas on the southern arena of the main shrine.

On the premise of Wakupati Narayan temple
A huge mass of people visits the temple at Ekadashi. Although, people stay up during the Nitya Puja as well. Each day, in the morn and on the eve, the Pujari of the temple performs daily worship. And to witness that, the nearby people especially the senior citizens gather over there.
Just within a while, you could see the gang of these older people on the premises of this temple who tend to laugh and gossiping in the patis (resthouse) of Suryamadhi, a minute before. They reach over there in such a perfect time as if it’s their daily routine to be there.
And of course, perceiving those glimpse of old people who shares a sort of stories with each other, including strangers like us really brings a smile to your face. Thus, It would be great if you could reach there in the evening, around 6 pm.
Also, there is a belief among the local denizens that if people sit in the courtyard while visiting the temple, the back pain is cured. It is like the blessing of God. So the people of Bhaktapur, still sit there at least once while visiting the temple, even if they are in a super hurry.
Wait, there is more to explore on the premises of this temple. Among several patis and minor temples from the premises, the pati from the end of the east corner consists of more exaggerating wooden artworks. It looks like leaving unavoidable crafting is a sign of the then Nepalese architecture.

The 55 Window Palace, also known as Pachpanna Jhyale Durbar in Nepali, is a historic palace located in Bhaktapur Durbar Square in Bhaktapur, Nepal. It was built during the reign of King Bhupatindra Malla in the 15th century and is considered one of the finest examples of traditional Newari architecture in Nepal.

The palace is named after its 55 intricately carved wooden windows, which are adorned with lattice work, statues of deities, and other decorative elements. The palace was originally used as a royal residence and a center for administration, and it was also the site of important ceremonies and events.

The 55 Window Palace is a three-story building with a central courtyard and a number of smaller rooms and chambers. The palace is built entirely from brick and timber, and its sloping roofs and ornate carvings are typical of Newari architecture. The palace is now a museum, where visitors can learn about the history of Bhaktapur and the Malla dynasty.

In addition to the 55 Window Palace, Bhaktapur Durbar Square is home to a number of other important structures, including the Golden Gate, the Taleju Temple, and the Natapole Temple, among others. The area is also known for its vibrant street life, with vendors selling traditional handicrafts, food, and other goods in the bustling squares and alleyways. Overall, Bhaktapur Durbar Square is a must-visit destination for anyone interested in Nepal's rich cultural heritage and history.

The 55 Window Palace (also known as Pachpanchhya Jhale) is a palace located in Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Nepal. It is a five-story palace with 55 intricately carved windows, hence the name. The palace was built in the 17th century by King Bhupatindra Malla and is considered one of the finest examples of Newari architecture.
The windows of the palace are made of sandalwood and are decorated with intricate carvings of flowers, animals, and other motifs. The palace also has a number of other features, including a courtyard, a water tank, and a library.
The 55 Window Palace was damaged in the 1934 earthquake, but it has since been restored. It is now a popular tourist destination and is one of the most photographed buildings in Bhaktapur.

When you consider that the palace was finished in 1754, under the rule of King Bhupatindra Malla, the 55 windows, constructed of black lacquered sandalwood, were extremely complex. Golden wing bird and Kali, the goddess of destruction, were 2 well-known figures that could be seen over the Golden Gate. The gate served as the principal entrance to the courtyard of the palace. Tamkey Dada(hill), a famous Hill Station in Eastern Nepal.
Tamkey is one of the most famous hills on the eastern hillside of Nepal. It is around 250 km to the east of Kathmandu(the Capital city of Nepal). Its height is around 3000meter from the sea level. It is one of the tallest hills of the Mahabharat Parbat range of Nepal. Geography, weather, cool temperature, and holy place for the people living around it add to its value.
Tamkey divides khotang and Bhojpur district, which belongs to one province of Nepal. Tamkey is surrounded by the greenery of beautiful flowers. The Laligurans( rhododendron, national flower of Nepal,), Chimal, Loths Sallha, Alpine Pine trees, Rhimchebung(the most described flower in Kirat's holy mundhum and myths), and thousands of medicinal plants surround this place. The air at the top is so fresh that it can refresh your mood, making people forget all the pain in their life. From the top of the Tamkey we can see the Himalayan range including Mount Everest to the north and tall himals. When the sunlight from the south hits the snow on the Himalayas, the beauties of mother nature can be seen there, the scenery can't be described in words. During the sunrise, before the fog rises, we can see the river Ganga, Kolkata city of India. The sunrise and sunset are the other scenes you should never miss, and these are the scenes 99% of people miss most of the time because of the cold temperature and lack of shelter nearby. But now people have started a homestay business there, which can add to the popularity of Tamkeys.
Mhaparung, Sylame, Mundhum Trail, Myung, and Chakhewa, are the other beautiful places around it. They have their importance.
Besides its beauty, it is rich in natural resources. We can find several iron extraction mines that were used to extract iron During the Rana Regime Period in the history of Nepal. We can find evidence of Iron mines that existed in the past.
Tamkey is not only a hill for the people living around it, but it represents their civilization. People have a strong belief in the holiness of these places. There is a temple at the top of the hill called siddhakali. The reality is that there is another real temple which is situated on a vertical slope. People can hardly get rich there, by analyzing the safety hazard, people made a temple on the hill. This place is a shared holy place where Kirat people living aro undthis place celebrate there on the

occasion of their festival called Sakela Ubhauli/Udhauli while other people celebrate on their festivals like buddha Jayanti/ Chandi Purnima, Shivaratri, Ram Navami. Thousands of generations have passed around this place so people's cultural and religious values are connected to it. This place resembles the history and civilization that happened in eastern hill Nepal.
Tamkey is almost equidistant from the District headquarters of Bhojpur and Bhojpur Bazar and Diktel, the district headquarter of Khotang. Madhya Pahadi Lokmarga(highway) passes close to this place. Construction of these highways has connected this beautiful palace to the other places of Nepal and the world. Now several roads connect this Place to terai Districts. review_text:
Me and my girlfriend decided to do a safari in between two hikes in Himalaya.
After a long research online we decided to give our trust to this company, and we didn’t regret it at all.
We are glad our final choice was The Chitwan Jungle Guides.
They’ve been extremely nice and professional since the beginning.
We opted for a 5 days 4 nights experience, with a private guide and private excursions.
Our guide was Narayan, a great guide and amazing person who has been working in Chitwan for more than 20 years. He knows all the birds and can recognise them by their sound. We spotted a lot of crocs, deers, rhinos, few elephants and traces of bears and tiger; unfortunately we weren’t able to see those last two, but we’ve been told in advance that December was the best season to spot those kind of animals.
We had one night booked in a tower in the jungle, that was epic epic.
Overall it’s been an extremely great tour, we lived properly a safari experience with experts, we’ve been safe and instructed to proper behaviour in a wild environment. That was great to see a huge respect for the nature and the wildlife from the guides.
We highly suggest to book with this company, and if you can ask for Narayan as your guide you’ll be very satisfied.
Good job everyone!!

The temple, perched on a hill, offers stunning panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, making it a popular pilgrimage destination and a scenic spot for visitors.

The architecture of the temple reflects traditional Nepali design, with intricate carvings and vibrant decorations that enhance its spiritual ambiance. The site is often bustling with devotees, especially during festivals, creating a lively atmosphere filled with prayer and celebration.

The trek to Dolakha Bhimsen is both rewarding and accessible, attracting not only pilgrims but also nature lovers who appreciate the tranquil environment and beautiful surroundings. The local community is warm and welcoming, providing visitors with insights into their customs and traditions.

Overall, Dolakha Bhimsen is a captivating blend of spirituality and natural beauty, making it a must-visit for those exploring the cultural and religious heritage of Nepal.

Dolakha Bhimsen Mandir is a sacred sanctuary that embodies centuries of devotion, tradition, and spiritual significance. Dedicated to the revered deity Bhimsen, this ancient temple holds a special place in the hearts of pilgrims and devotees who flock here seeking blessings and solace.
As you approach Dolakha Bhimsen Mandir, you are greeted by the sight of its towering pagoda-style architecture, adorned with intricate carvings and vibrant colors. The temple's imposing presence against the backdrop of the Himalayas instills a sense of reverence and awe, setting the stage for a truly transformative experience.
Stepping into the temple grounds, you are enveloped in an atmosphere of tranquility and devotion. The air is filled with the melodious chants of prayers and the fragrance of incense, creating a sacred ambiance that transports you to a realm of spirituality.
The sanctum sanctorum, where the idol of Bhimsen resides, is the heart of the temple. Here, devotees offer prayers, perform rituals, and seek blessings for prosperity and protection. The energy within the temple is palpable, as the fervent devotion of the worshippers reverberates through its halls.
Beyond its religious significance, Dolakha Bhimsen Mandir is also steeped in history and legend. Stories abound about the miraculous powers of Bhimsen and the temple's role in protecting the local community from adversity. These tales add depth and mystique to the temple's allure, inviting visitors to delve deeper into its rich heritage.
Surrounding the temple are breathtaking vistas of the Himalayan landscape, offering a serene backdrop for contemplation and reflection. Whether you're a devout pilgrim, a curious traveler, or simply a seeker of spiritual nourishment, Dolakha Bhimsen Mandir welcomes you with open arms, inviting you to embark on a journey of discovery and enlightenment.
In conclusion, Dolakha Bhimsen Mandir is not just a temple; it is a sacred sanctuary where faith meets beauty.

The central hill district of Dolakha is naturally and culturally sublime. Mount Gaurishankar, based on which the Nepal Standard Time is determined, and the Rolwaling mountain range, stand tall in the north. The winding Tamakoshi River whistles down south and pours into the Koshi river. Kalinchok Bhagwati Temple, known for snowfall during the winter, is revered by the locals as the “shrine of the district”.

Charikot, the district headquarters of Dolakha, is around 133 km east of Kathmandu. Travel along the Araniko Highway until you reach Khadichaur, from where the serpentine road climbs through rural settlements and terraced farmlands. Aahaldanda in Lakuridanda welcomes you to Dolakha territory and leads to Kharidhunga which overlooks Rolwaling and Langtang mountain ranges. Kharidhunga, situated at an altitude of around 2,700 metres above sea level, is covered with powdery snow throughout winter. The rhododendron forests colour the area red as spring sets in.

What can I say, but my 15-day trek to Mt Everest Base Camp was life revealing.  I was supposed to be on a senior trek with 3 other people, but they postponed their trip, so I was by myself.  I remember Naresh recommending that from the beginning, and he was right... it was the best option for me.  Naresh also helped me plan a trip to Pokhara before the trek.  He was always so quickly available to answer my questions, concerns, or emails.  For the trek, I was blessed with the companionship of Jhit Lama as my guide and Krishna as my porter.  They took exceptional care of me.  I felt secure and confident in their lead.  I celebrated my 70th birthday on the trip.  I am in fairly decent shape, but I was a little leary of what might come.  Well, the altitude did affect me.  It made me both euphoric and emotional, and there was one night I couldn't breathe or felt that I couldn't.   My mind started putting me in panic mode, and it took everything to calm myself.  Jhit and Krishna comforted me, and actually, I believe, helped "will" me up the mountain.  We made it to Base Camp step by step, and I credit Jhit and Krishna for that.  The desending, Jhit said would be easier, and it was.  My lungs felt relief as we lowered our elevation.  Jhit and Krishna even took the time to celebrate my birthday with a yummy cake and other surprises!  Hand in hand, we made it down some slippery slopes, and along the way, we shared snacks, laughter, and our lives.  Jhit was fantastic as he was kind, compassionate and gentle, yet strong, and always in command of the trek. Krishna was more than a porter as he often walked behind me, always prepared to lend a hand or give a helpful push.  I will forever be grateful and value them as very special friends.  I learned much from the trek.  I learned how to accept help, support and, along the way, I discovered my own self-worth.  The trek, as it turned out, was never about the end goal, but the journey and with these guys by my side I could not go wrong.  I want to thank Jhit, Krishna, and all the players in Himalayan Scenery Treks and Expedition, Naresh and Sonu, for treating me as more than just a client, but as family.  I highly recommend them to anyone considering exploring the beauty of Nepal

And when trekking back downhill, back to Sayabrubesi where we started this adventure, the most beautiful butterflies were guiding me back and they let me see the path I took. Accessible through a trekking trail from the district headquarters, Todke Jharana promises a captivating experience for nature enthusiasts and adventure seekers alike. During my recent visit, I was mesmerized by the sheer grandeur and tranquility of this captivating waterfall.

Awe-Inspiring Natural Wonder:
Todke Jharana is a true spectacle of nature's power and beauty. As the water plunges from great heights, it creates a mesmerizing display of cascading streams that captivate the senses. The roar of the waterfall, coupled with the mist-filled air, creates an ambiance that evokes a sense of wonder and awe. Standing in its presence, one can't help but feel humbled by the magnificence of the natural world.

Trekking Adventure:
Reaching Todke Jharana requires embarking on a trekking adventure, which adds to the allure of the experience. The trail leading to the waterfall is surrounded by lush greenery, offering panoramic views of the rolling hills and verdant landscapes of Ilam. The journey itself becomes an integral part of the overall experience, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty of the region.

Tourism Development Efforts:
The local government has recognized the potential of Todke Jharana as a tourist attraction and has taken steps to enhance the visitor experience. Efforts are underway to develop roads and lodging facilities near the waterfall, making it more accessible and comfortable for tourists. These initiatives will undoubtedly contribute to the growth of tourism in the area, allowing more people to witness the captivating beauty of Todke Jharana.

Nature's Retreat:
Todke Jharana offers a serene retreat for those seeking solace amidst nature's embrace. The surrounding tranquility and the sound of rushing water create a soothing atmosphere that washes away the stress of everyday life. Visitors can find respite by sitting near the waterfall, listening to its gentle melody, and basking in the serenity of the surroundings. It's a perfect spot to unwind, reflect, and reconnect with nature.

Conclusion:
Todke Jharana, nestled in the hills of Maimajhuwa near Mai Pokhari, is a majestic natural wonder that leaves a lasting impression. With its impressive height and captivating beauty, the waterfall offers a mesmerizing experience for adventurers and nature lovers. The ongoing tourism development efforts by the local government will further enhance the accessibility and infrastructure around the waterfall. If you are seeking a tranquil escape surrounded by the splendor of nature, Todke Jharana in Ilam district is a destination that should not be missed.

Guheshwari Temple: A Sacred Abode of Divine Power

Located just 1km east of the revered Pashupatinath Temple, on the southern bank of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Nepal, Guheshwari Temple stands as a testament to the profound spiritual heritage of the region.

At the heart of this holy site lies the deity Mahadevi Guhyekali, symbolizing the primordial Aadhi Shakti, or Divine Power. The temple's energy dynamics, intricately linked with its proximity to the Pashupatinath Temple, add to its spiritual significance, drawing devout tantric worshipers seeking divine blessings.

Originally built in the pagoda style, the temple was meticulously renovated in the 17th century by King Pratap Malla, preserving its architectural splendor for generations to come.

Guheshwari Temple comes alive during its main festivals, such as Chaitra Dashain, Bada Dashain, and Navratri, when devotees flock to pay homage to the divine feminine energy embodied within its sacred walls.

Legend intertwines with mythology at Guheshwari Temple, as it is believed to mark the spot where Sati Devi, in her fury at the disrespect shown to her husband Shiva by her father Daksha, immolated herself. Unable to bear her loss, Shiva carried her body, and as her divine form disintegrated, her body parts fell to earth, creating the 51 Shakti Peeths. Guheshwari Temple stands as a testament to this myth, marking the place where Sati Devi's hips fell, infusing the site with the divine power of the universe.

For centuries, Guheshwari Temple has been a focal point of spiritual reverence, drawing pilgrims and seekers from far and wide to bask in its divine aura and connect with the primal energy that permeates its sacred precincts.

Rara is considered as the land where "Apsara-most beautiful deity of Indralok (holy place in heaven according to Hindu apprehension)" has landed. It is a big lake in a pristine area very very far from chaos and crowd of the town. It might take ages to travel here from Kathmandu. There are various ways to reach here. 1. Booking jeep from Kathmandu to reach here. 2. Direct flight from Kathmandu to Talcha Airport. 3. Flight from Ktm to Nepalgunj and reserve jeep to Rara. 4. Flight from Ktm to Surkhet and travel in jeep reservation. Other than these ideas if you have lot of travel time and want to go comfortably without hectic schedule, you can take a bus from Ktm to surkhet (1 day) stay a night there, go to Kalikot nagma (1day), and reach Rara on the 3rd day via Jumla and Mugu.
Once you start to reach there, you either go to Rara lake from Salleri in horse or walking via airport area by 1hour hike. There are hotels in Salleri and Talcha Airport. Be sure to book hotels as there are no hotels after this 1hr hike. After that you have choice of going across the lake by about 2hrs hike or about half year boat ride conducted by Nepali Army. It will take you about 3-4hrs hike for whole round of the lake depending on your walking speed. There are no roads for 2 wheelers and 4 wheelers once you reach rara lake. You can also go across by Horse which will take you about NRs. 1000. Once you reach across you can stay at Danphe hotel or Heritage hotel again run by the nepali army. They have ok kind of food and ok kind of hospitality. But you have no other choices than that. But the view of the lake mountains and night sky is no doubt breathtaking. "Chyangra" meat is special here with apple wine. Every Nepali must go there at least once even though the travel makes you wanna give up. I strongly recommend all to go there during autumn season or spring season as the roads in Jumla, Kalikot and Mugu are very dangerous which have claimed hundreds of lives in road accidents. During this season you can also see lots of biodiversities like butterflies, flowers and birds. The scenary is also pretty beautiful and we can also see the water changing different colors in a single day.

Like a resplendent new bride adorned in exquisite makeup, the park exudes a mesmerizing allure, gracefully nestled on the banks of the majestic Karnali River, eagerly awaiting its groom.

A symphony of colours awaits visitors at Tikapur Park, where hundreds of flowers burst into vibrant blooms, creating a kaleidoscope of reds, whites, blacks, pinks, yellows, greens, and more. Each step taken through this floral wonderland feels like a brushstroke on a living canvas, painting an unforgettable memory in the minds of those who wander its paths.

He made sure to give us tips each day on what kind of food to eat, appropriately dressing up/down as per the predicted weather which was really critical. Every day with him was a joy! His lighthearted jokes and stories made some gruelling parts of the trek a breeze. He truly made sure our trek to ABC was a dream realised. It doesn't matter if you are a beginner or an experienced trekker, the experience Bishnu Ji comes with and his personable nature is bound to make your experience a real special one. Kori Dada is a popular hiking destination in Nepal.It offers panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges, making it a favored spot for sunrise and sunset views. The hike itself is relatively easy to moderate, suitable for beginners and experienced trekkers alike.The route is less crowded compared to more well-known treks, which adds to its charm for nature lovers looking for a peaceful escape. Along the way, hikers pass through traditional Gurung villages, terraced farmlands, and lush forests. The simplicity of the rural lifestyle, combined with the breathtaking scenery, makes the trek a cultural and scenic experience.

**Review: Kori, Kaski District – A Hidden Gem for Trekking Enthusiasts**

Nestled in the scenic Kaski district, Kori is an enchanting destination for trekkers seeking a more tranquil, off-the-beaten-path experience in the Annapurna region. The journey to Kori begins from Sikles village, a charming settlement known for its traditional culture and stunning vistas. The trek takes about 1.5 days, winding through lush rhododendron forests and offering glimpses of the majestic Himalayan range along the way.

The route to Kori is a gradual ascent, perfect for trekkers looking for a moderate challenge. As you traverse the forested trails, the vibrant colors of blooming rhododendrons create a breathtaking landscape, especially during springtime. The path is well-marked and relatively peaceful, providing a serene trekking experience compared to more crowded routes like Poon Hill or Annapurna Base Camp.

Once you reach Kori, the panoramic views make the journey worthwhile. The snow-capped peaks of Annapurna IV, Lamjung Himal, and the iconic Machapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) rise majestically against the sky, creating a dramatic backdrop that will leave you in awe. The area offers fantastic photo opportunities, especially at sunrise and sunset, when the mountains are bathed in golden light.

Along the way, there are a few basic yet welcoming eateries and cottages that provide food and lodging. While the accommodations are simple, they offer a warm atmosphere where you can rest, recharge, and interact with the friendly locals. The meals, often made from locally sourced ingredients, are hearty and provide the perfect fuel for the trek ahead.

Kori remains relatively under the radar compared to other trekking destinations in Nepal, making it a great choice for those looking to escape the crowds and immerse themselves in nature. Whether you're a seasoned trekker or a beginner, the journey to Kori is rewarding both physically and spiritually, offering a perfect combination of natural beauty and mountain serenity.

In summary, if you're in search of a peaceful trekking adventure with stunning mountain views and a close connection to nature, Kori is a must-visit destination in Kaski district. It's a perfect blend of natural beauty, local culture, and an immersive trekking experience that will stay with you long after your journey ends.

Embarking on a trek to Kori from Sikles is an adventure that showcases the raw beauty of nature, presenting challenges and rewards along the way. Here's a guide to help you plan your trek to this "heaven on earth":

Trekking Route and Time
- Sikles to Tasha: The trek starts from Sikles village, taking approximately 5 hours to reach Tasha. Another account suggests a steeper uphill trek can take about 4.5 to 5 hours.
- Tasha to Kori: From Tasha, expect a challenging journey of about 7 to 8 hours to reach Kori. This part of the trek involves steep uphills and, depending on the season, about 3 hours of walking on snow.

Weather and Precautions
- Weather Considerations: The weather can turn harsh post-midday, making a raincoat essential regardless of the season. Experiencing live snowfall is a possibility, adding to the trek's allure.
- Water Supply: Water sources are limited, emphasizing the need to carry sufficient water bottles.
- Leeches: During summer, leeches can be a nuisance, requiring trekkers to take necessary precautions.

Accommodation
- Limited Lodging: The trekking route has limited hotel options, making advance booking advisable to secure accommodation.

Scenic Beauty
- Panoramic Views: On clear days, the trek rewards with stunning views, including the majestic Annapurna and Manaslu mountain ranges. Kori itself is praised for its breathtaking vistas and is deemed very beautiful when the weather is favorable.
- Seasonal Changes: The landscape of Kori Hill and its surroundings undergo dramatic transformations with the seasons, each offering a distinct charm and beauty. Greenery may not always be present, but every season imbues the area with its unique splendor.

Cultural and Spiritual Sites
- Cultural Significance: The route is not just a trekking adventure but also a cultural journey through Gurung native places and pilgrimage sites, enriching the experience beyond physical activity.

In summary, the trek from Sikles to Kori is an enriching experience that combines physical challenges with the serene beauty of nature and the rich cultural tapestry of Nepal. It's an adventure that requires preparation, respect for nature, and an openness to the elements, promising a rewarding journey for those who undertake it.

review_text:
Panauti is a historical city in Nepal, originally it was a small state given by King Bhupatindra Malla as a dowry to his sister. This town has a population of under 15,000 people and a few prominent icons, such as the Indreswor temple and Panauti (Layaku) Durbar square found in the town center. At the end of the 13th century, Panauti was finally integrated into the unified kingdom of Nepal, along with Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur, which are all former capital cities of the Kathmandu valley. Panauti was a trading hub along the ancient Salt Trade route between Tibet and India. Actually, the recorded history of Panauti goes back to the first century AD. However, with the end of the Salt trade in the 1950s and the construction of the Arniko Highway in the 1960s bypassing this old town, Panauti has gone into an economic rut. Panauti, consists of a variety of Buddhist and Hindu religious monuments, and is considered to be one of the area's most important medieval sites. Panauti is also steeped in culture and tradition. Visitors will often find colorful stones, petals and other items that are laid out on the pavement to welcome everyone with great hospitality.
Panauti, situated at the confluence of the two rivers Rosi and Punyamati, has been regarded as an important religious site since very early times. In Nepali society, such rivers are considered to be sacred. A visit or just an ablution to such places enables the visitor to be freed from many sins and anxieties, as it is believed to be sacred. Moreover, it is also believed that at Panauti, in addition to aforesaid two rivers, a third river Lilawati also converges making it again a tri-junction called Triveni. However, the last one is said to be visible only to the sheers and the intellectuals. The presence of this at Panauti has added and remarkably enhanced its religious sanctity and popularity as well. On account of this, every festive occasion, a great number of devotees from all across the country pour here for a holy ablution and to pay homage to the nearby Indreshwor Mahadev Temple and other holy sites located here. The site is also regarded as Prayagtirtha of Nepal.

Balkumari Picnic Spot is a beautiful and popular picnic spot located in Lalitpur District, Nepal. It is situated on a hilltop overlooking the Kathmandu Valley, and offers stunning views of the surrounding mountains and cityscape.

The picnic spot is well-maintained, with plenty of space to spread out and relax. There are also several shelters and gazebos where you can eat and drink out of the sun. There is also a children's playground, making it a great place for families to visit.

In addition to the picnic area, Balkumari Picnic Spot also has a temple dedicated to the Hindu goddess Balkumari. The temple is a popular pilgrimage site, and many people visit to pray and make offerings to the goddess.

Here is a review of Balkumari Picnic Spot:

**Pros:**

* Beautiful scenery with stunning views of the Kathmandu Valley and surrounding mountains.
* Well-maintained picnic area with plenty of space to spread out and relax.
* Shelters and gazebos to eat and drink out of the sun.
* Children's playground.
* Temple dedicated to the Hindu goddess Balkumari.

**Cons:**

* Can be crowded on weekends and holidays.
* Some of the shelters and gazebos are in need of repair.
* The road to the picnic spot can be narrow and winding.

Overall, Balkumari Picnic Spot is a great place to visit for a picnic, hike, or to simply relax and enjoy the views. It is especially popular on weekends and holidays, so it is best to visit early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid the crowds.

**Tips for visiting Balkumari Picnic Spot:**

* Bring your own food and drinks, as there are limited food options available at the picnic spot.
* Wear comfortable shoes and clothing, as you will likely be doing a lot of walking.
* Bring a hat and sunscreen to protect yourself from the sun.
* Be aware of the monkeys that live in the area. They can be aggressive, so it is best to keep your food and belongings close to you.
* If you are visiting on a weekend or holiday, be prepared for crowds.

A site with great historical importance. The place is linked with the starting of the Shah Dynasty that ruled over Nepal until monarchy was abolished recently.  It was the palace of the King of Lamjung, yashobrahma Shah, who was the son of Kulamandal Shah Khand, the king of Kaski. Since there was no King in Lamjung at the time, the people went to Kaski to request Kulamandal Shah to allow them to choose one among the princes of Kaski to be taken to Lamjung Kingdom and crowned as their King. Yashobrahma Shah was chosen and taken to Lamjung by Khajedura of Duradanda and was crowned the King of Lamjung. the descendant of Yashobrahma Shah, Drabya Shah later became the King of Gorkha by winning an annual race that took place for selection of King of Gorkha every year. Dravya Shah is also the ancestor of King Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha kingdom, who is responsible for initiating  the formation of Nepal by concurring many small kingdoms as we know today.

Makwanpur Gadhi, a historic fortress located in Makwanpur district of Nepal, is a significant site with cultural and historical importance. Built in the 16th century by the Sen dynasty, it served as a strategic military stronghold and a center of governance. Surrounded by lush forests and elevated terrain, Makwanpur Gadhi offers scenic views and a glimpse into Nepal’s medieval architecture. Today, it attracts visitors interested in history, architecture, and the legacy of Nepal's unification period.

A Sacred Haven of Peace and Spiritual Unity

CG Temple, known as Shashwat Dham, located in the tranquil Devchuli Municipality of Nawalpur District, is an extraordinary place that truly embodies spiritual harmony. The temple is part of the larger CG Industrial Park owned by the Chaudhary Group, and since its inauguration in 2017 by Nepal's President Bidhya Devi Bhandari, it has grown to become a major spiritual and tourist destination in Nepal.

I had the privilege of visiting this magnificent temple and was captivated by its serene atmosphere. During my visit, I was able to capture some beautiful pictures of the Buddha and Mahavira statues, which stand as symbols of peace, wisdom, and non  violence. These statues are beautifully crafted and positioned within a well  maintained temple complex, creating a perfect setting for those who are interested in photography or simply wish to connect with the deeper meanings behind these spiritual figures.

The entire temple complex is a blend of Hindu and Buddhist elements, reflecting Nepal’s rich cultural heritage and religious inclusiveness. One can find not only a Hindu temple but also a Buddhist stupa, all surrounded by lush greenery, making the environment ideal for meditation, relaxation, and spiritual reflection.

What Makes CG Temple Special:
@   Spiritual and Architectural Marvel  : The temple complex seamlessly integrates Hindu and Buddhist elements, with stunning statues, shrines, and a peaceful stupa. The architecture is modern yet infused with traditional spiritual elements.
@   Buddha and Mahavira Statues  : These impressive statues exude tranquility and can be found in peaceful corners of the temple, providing excellent photographic opportunities.
@   Serenity and Calm  : Whether you're a pilgrim, a spiritual seeker, or a casual visitor, the temple offers an atmosphere of peace and calm that immediately soothes the mind and soul.
@   Cultural and Historical Significance  : Shashwat Dham has already won awards as one of the best tourist destinations in Nepal, with easy access from the Mahendra Highway for those traveling to sacred sites like Lumbini or Chitwan National Park
@   Open for All  : The temple complex is open daily from 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM, and the best time to visit is in the evening between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM, when the atmosphere is especially serene.

A Few Practical Tips:
No Entrance Fees: While the temple grounds are free to enter, there is a nominal fee of NPR 100 for visiting the museum in the center of the park, which is worth it if you're interested in Nepalese history and spirituality.
@Accommodations: For those who wish to extend their visit, there are homestays and hotels nearby in Dumkauli or Daldale, offering a chance to fully immerse in the peaceful surroundings.

Overall, CG Temple (Shashwat Dham) is a place of spiritual and architectural beauty that leaves a lasting impression. Whether you come for prayer, meditation, or simply to admire the stunning craftsmanship of the Buddha and Mahavira statues, this temple provides an enriching and peaceful experience that is not to be missed. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Nepal!

Shree Bhairabi Temple, located in Nuwakot, Nepal, is a sacred Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Bhairabi, an incarnation of Goddess Durga. Situated on a hill, the temple offers breathtaking views of the surrounding area, including Nuwakot Durbar. Known for its traditional Nepali pagoda-style architecture, the temple features intricate wood carvings and symbolic Hindu art. It holds great religious significance and attracts devotees seeking blessings for protection and prosperity. The temple is especially vibrant during the Dashain festival, where rituals and sacrifices are performed to honor the goddess, symbolizing the victory of good over evil. Shree Bhairabi Temple is a cultural and spiritual landmark in Nepal.

Shree Bhairabi Temple, Nuwakot: A Divine Encounter
Shree Bhairabi Temple, perched atop a hill overlooking the picturesque Nuwakot district, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Nepal. The temple's serene ambiance and the devotion of the worshippers create a truly spiritual experience.
The temple's architecture is a blend of traditional Newari and Hindu styles. The intricate carvings on the temple walls and the towering gopuram (entrance tower) are a sight to behold. The main deity, Goddess Bhairabi, is known for her fierce form and her ability to protect against evil.
The temple's location, surrounded by lush greenery and offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscape, adds to its charm. The peaceful atmosphere and the chanting of mantras create a sense of tranquility. Visitors can witness various rituals and ceremonies performed by the temple's priests.
One of the highlights of my visit was witnessing the evening aarti, a sacred ritual involving the lighting of lamps and the offering of prayers to the deity. The collective devotion of the worshippers was truly inspiring.
Shree Bhairabi Temple is not just a religious site but also a cultural hub. The temple's annual festival, Bhairabi Jatra, is a major event attracting thousands of devotees from across the country.
If you're seeking a spiritual retreat or simply want to experience the beauty of Nepalese culture, Shree Bhairabi Temple is a must-visit. The temple's serene ambiance, rich history, and the devotion of the worshippers make it a truly unforgettable experience.

Nestled in the serene hills of Palpa, Bhairabsthan Temple stands as a revered religious site with deep historical and cultural significance located about 10 km north west from the city of Tansen, in Palpa district of Nepal at an elevation of about 1470 m. Hindu people worship at the temple mainly in Mahaastami of Dashain. During the festivals, animal sacrifices (buffalo, goat, sheep and rooster) are performed in the temple. Pancha Bali is also performed, which involves the sacrifice of five kinds of animals namely buffalo, goat, sheep, rooster and duck. The temple is famous for the iconic trident which is considered as the biggest in Nepal. Dedicated to Bhairab, a fearsome incarnation of Lord Shiva, the temple is an important pilgrimage destination for devotees and visitors alike, offering both spiritual solace and a panoramic view of the surrounding landscape.
The temple is also surrounded by dense forests, adding to its tranquil atmosphere. As you approach the temple, the view of the surrounding valleys, rivers, and distant snow-capped mountains makes for a perfect backdrop, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in both natural beauty and spirituality.
Devotees visit to seek blessings for protection, strength, and the removal of obstacles in their lives. It is believed that Lord Bhairab, known for his wrathful nature, helps to drive away evil forces and ensures the safety and well-being of his devotees.
One of the most remarkable features of the Bhairabsthan Temple is the stunning panoramic view from the temple’s premises. From the top of the hill, you can enjoy breathtaking views of Palpa’s valleys, the Kali Gandaki River, and even distant snow-capped peaks. The temple is particularly beautiful at sunrise and sunset when the light casts a golden glow over the landscape, making it a perfect spot for photography and reflection.

Bhairabsthan Temple is more than just a place of worship; it is a serene retreat that offers visitors a glimpse into the spiritual and cultural heart of Nepal. Whether you are visiting for religious reasons, to admire the stunning scenery, or simply to experience the peaceful atmosphere, this temple is a hidden gem that should not be missed when in Palpa.

Kal Bhairab Temple (Bhairabsthan) is one of the biggest hindu temple of lord Kal Bhairab (Bhairav) . It is located about 8 KM from Tansen, district headquarter in between Tansen Tamghas road on the hill of Bhairabsthan VDC, in the mid western part of Palpa District, Nepal. This temple was build by Pratam Samser Rana. This temple has the biggest trident (trishul) of asia.
The main statue of Lord Bhairab is kept hidden because it's sight is unbearable and frightening. There's a copy of the main statue which people can see and worship. The myth says that, whosoever catch a glimpse of the main statue are in danger of loosing their life. The priest (aka Jogi) also worship the statue from behind the curtain. These in also the Mai goddess temple in the same facility.

The main days for worshiping this temple is Tuesdays and Saturdays. Beside that many pilgrims come to visit this temple in the month of Mangsir (Nov-Dec). The busiest day of the temple is on the day of Maha Ashtami of Navaratra.

The main parsad of this temple is "Rot", which is made up of wheat flour. "Rot" is a secret rice bread that can be eaten after it has been worshiped in the temple. Animal sacrifice is also done in this temple. Goat , Rooster, and male Buffalow are the animals sacrificed in this temple. Different kind of animal sacrifice called "Pancha Bali" (five animal sacrifice is also done in this temple.)

Literally Pancha Bali Means Sacrifice of five kinds of animals, buffalo, goat, sheep, hen and duck. Only the males of these animals can be sacrificed in the shrines of gods and goddesses. After the fulfillment of the wish, a day is fixed for Pancha Bali, according to lunar calendar. Generally the eight-day of the new moon or full moon day is preferred.

To offer Pancha Bali people go to the temple from their house in processions. A music band called Pancha Baja of local musicians heads the procession. At the temple the god or goddess is worshipped ceremoniously and the animals and bird are sacrificed one by one. Generally the buffalo is given to the members of the musical band.

Since the temple is on the top of the hill, you can see the beautiful range of Mt. Machhapuchhre, Mt. Annapurna and Mt. Dhaulagiri.

Degree Shaikumari Bhagwati Devi Temple Karnali Province Rukum (West) District Musikot Municipality Ward No. 5 Tharpu is an important religious and tourist site of Nepal. It has been a legend that Satya Shaikumari Bhagwati Devi Mandir has been named because she is a goddess who fulfills the desires of her heart and because she is a goddess who separates truth from falsehood.
Because of the same legend, remembering this Shaikumari Bhagwati Devi temple and vowing to fulfill their wishes and desires, thousands of pilgrims come to this temple every year to fulfill their vows after watching various auspicious scenes.
Every year from Haribodhani Ekadashi to Kartik Shukla Purnima, the degree fair is completed after the locals (Sagal) rotate sticks and perform parikarma.
More than 100,000 pilgrims visit the temple for five consecutive days to fill the fair and perform puja. Only on the last day of the fair, about 50,000 people visit the fair. Millions of people are traded in the fair.
Thousands of people from the neighboring districts of Rolpa, Dolpa, Salyan, Jajarkot, Pyuthan, Dang, Pyuthan, Surkhet, Banke, along with locals from Rukum (West-East) come to visit the temple and visit the temple, which is a unique confluence of local art-culture and dance-song. Visitors arrive.
A goat is also sacrificed here every year in gratitude for the fulfillment of one's vows. From the first day of the fair to the last day, it is customary to offer sacrifices in the temple premises, but at other times, sacrifices are also offered in the temple.
You can go to this temple from Bhandarikanda on the Madhyapahari highway and from the Math in the headquarters of Khalanga. If the level of the road could be improved, the number of tourists would increase.

The temple, which dates back to the 3rd century BC, is a simple structure featuring a sacred garden and a sacred pond. Inside the temple, a marker indicates the exact spot where Maya Devi is said to have given birth to the Buddha. The site is surrounded by lush greenery and attracts thousands of visitors and devotees each year, making it an important center for Buddhist spirituality and heritage.

Sindhuligadhi Memorial Park is a historically significant site in Sindhuli, Nepal, commemorating the bravery and sacrifices made during the battle of Sindhuligadhi. This battle, fought in 1767 between the Gorkha soldiers under the leadership of King Prithvi Narayan Shah and the forces of the Malla kings of Kathmandu Valley, played a crucial role in the unification of Nepal.

For history enthusiasts and those interested in Nepal's unification period, Sindhuligadhi Memorial Park provides a poignant and educational experience, allowing visitors to connect with the nation's rich past.

The Sindhuligadi Memorial Park is a public park located in Sindhuli, Nepal. It is a popular destination for locals and tourists alike, and it is known for its beautiful gardens, peaceful atmosphere, and cultural and historical significance.

The Sindhuligadi Memorial Park is located on the banks of the Kamala River, in the heart of Sindhuli. It covers an area of about 10 acres and is home to a number of attractions, including a large pond, walking paths, and a number of beautifully landscaped gardens. The park is also home to a number of memorials and statues that commemorate important figures and events in Nepal's history.

One of the most popular attractions in the Sindhuligadi Memorial Park is the Sindhuligadi Museum, which is dedicated to the history and culture of Sindhuli and the surrounding region. The museum houses a collection of artifacts, documents, and photographs that showcase the cultural and historical richness of the area. Visitors can learn about the history of the region, including its art, literature, and traditional crafts.

In addition to its cultural and historical significance, the Sindhuligadi Memorial Park is also an important recreational and leisure destination. It is a popular place for locals to come and relax, and it is a great place for tourists to experience the beauty and culture of Nepal. The park is open to the public from 7 am to 5 pm

Sindhuligadhi War Museum is the first war museum of Nepal. It is located in Kamalamai Municipality.

The museum has well preserved the weapons, artifacts, clothes etc. when the forces of British India arrived in Sindhuli Gadhi, the Gorkha military conducted a guerrilla attack against them. Many of the British Indian forces were killed and the rest eventually fled, leaving behind a huge amount of weapons and ammunition, which were seized by the Gorkha army.

Gorkha army under Banshu Gurung's command had prevented the British troops from advancing towards the Kathmandu Valley.

Gorkhas had used unconventional war tactics like unleashing the hornets and using nettles, among a variety of other tactics, to defeat the British soldiers

Getting to visit the first war museum of Nepal was really amazing. It was really cool to see all the techniques and weapons that the people used to fend off the attackers in the past. Outside of the museum, the place was really chill and peaceful (ironic since its WAR museum haha)

Sindhuligadhi War Museum is constructed very well. We can find historical artifacts, weapons, galleries, ancient accessories and many more. Sano Gadhi and Thulo Gadhi are major attractions. The museum area is kept clean, and organized with availability of all facilities. Ticket price is Rs. 50 per person and parking charge is Rs.10.

It is a historic battlefield won by the Nepal Army in a fierce battle with the army of the 'East India Company' led by Captain Kinlock, who was advancing towards Kathmandu in support of the then Malla King Jayaprakash Malla of Kathmandu during the unification of Nepal.  Sindhuligadhi Museum The Nepal Army has built a war museum in the Sindhuligadhi fort, which has historical significance after defeating the army of the East India Company.
The museum houses war weapons used by the ancestors to protect Nepal and old materials that can be kept in the war museum with the Nepal Army.  Sindhuligadhi has a history of defeating the British army equipped with modern weapons led by Captain Kinlock of the East India Company to capture Kathmandu in the battle of Sindhuligadhi on 15 September 1824 BS.  This war museum has also been established to develop Sindhuligadhi as an internationally recognized tourist destination.
Inside the War Museum are archives depicting the historical and strategic significance of the fort through artefacts, home-made weapons, cannons, ammunition, documents used by the army at that time, display of uniforms of the army and the opposition during the war.

Tarahara Bazar, (तरहरा बजार) commonly known as Behibare Bazar (विहिवारे बजार). Behibare (विहिवार) means Thursday (विहिवार) and Bazar (बजार) means Market in Nepali/Nepalese language.
*
Present (विहिवारे बजार) Thursday weekly market began more than 4 decade ago with the help of few local men working for the better and well being of our local community of Tarahara. 4 decade ago our founding fathers of Tarahara would have never imagined Behibare of today. Yet in their heart they had simple but a genuine love and care for their local community economically and socially.
*
It was the beginning of small things but was a sincere one. Which motivated them to encourage both local and neighbouring village vendors to come and sell essential produces like green vegetables, potatoes, radish, tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger, rice, lentils, as well as other daily essential household products like cooking oil, kerosene for lamp, washing soap, salt, sugar etc. It took a lot to convince these weekly vendors to come and sell their products and as the time went on Behibare Bazar began to grow rapidly which saw additional market day, Monday as well to be a weekly bazar day. Today, we have Thursday and Monday as weekly bazar day, but it is till called as Behibare Bazar, still called by it first market day of the week.
*
For more info and photos visit: EasternNepal.com/tarahara

KakreBihar in Surkhet District, Nepal, is a hidden gem that offers a unique blend of history, spirituality, and natural beauty. This ancient Hindu-Buddhist temple, built in the 12th century, stands majestically on a small hill in Latikoili , providing a serene and picturesque setting.

The temple’s architecture is a marvel, constructed from solid stone with intricate bronze idols of Hindu gods and goddesses, as well as Buddha. The restoration efforts completed in 2021 have beautifully preserved its historical essence while making it more accessible to visitors1. The site spans over 180 hectares, offering ample space for exploration and reflection.

Visiting KakreBihar is not just about the temple itself but also about the journey. The surrounding landscape is lush and green, with panoramic views of the Surkhet Valley. The moderate climate makes it a pleasant destination year-round. Whether you’re a history enthusiast, a spiritual seeker, or simply someone who appreciates natural beauty, KakreBihar has something to offer.

The peaceful ambiance of the temple grounds is perfect for meditation and relaxation. The local community is welcoming, and you can often find knowledgeable guides who can share fascinating stories about the temple’s history and significance. There are also several spots nearby for picnics and leisurely walks, making it a great place for families and solo travelers alike.

In summary, KakreBihar is a must-visit destination in Surkhet District. Its rich history, stunning architecture, and tranquil environment make it a perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life. Highly recommended for anyone traveling through Karnali Province!

Wow! What's a Place? Actually, this Vihar located in the provincial capital of Karnali Province in western Nepal is a good tourist destination.
A 10-minute drive from Birendranagar in Surkhet, through a road passing through green forests, this Bihar in Chure is very charming.  This shikhar style temple looks medieval and makes everyone happy.

Since its discovery about 50 years ago, the Kakrebihar site has attracted the interest of archaeologists and Buddhist scholars. They agree that it dates back to the 13th-14th century, but question whether it is truly a Buddhist site or a Hindu temple that adopted Buddhist characteristics.

Was it one of the many places on the prehistoric route that passed through the Surkhet-Dang region through the vital Gangetic plains to the south? Who built it — the followers of Vajrayana Buddhism in the Kathmandu Valley or the Tibetan Buddhism in the mountains? And was it also built as a temple, or could it have been a palace, monastery or something else?

Kankrebihar Ruins is the largest Buddhist Bihar in ruins in Nepal. It was built in the 12th century and it spreads over 180 hectares of land. The temple was restored in September 2021.

review_text:
The place is a good starting point for anyone interested in science, but it feels like there’s a lot of untapped potential. The overall experience is fairly basic, with limited things to observe compared to what you’d expect from such a large facility. While the building itself is impressive in size, there aren’t many ongoing projects or interactive displays, which leaves you wanting more.

For science students or enthusiasts, this can still be a worthwhile visit, especially if you're in a group or on a school trip. There are several interesting gadgets and exhibits scattered around, but the collection isn’t quite enough to fully immerse you. A bit more hands-on activities or cutting-edge technological innovations could really enhance the experience and make it more engaging.

The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, but there’s a sense that the center is still developing or unfinished. They have plans for a planetarium, which could be a big draw once it’s completed, but as it stands, the place feels like it’s missing that next level of innovation and interactivity that could turn it into a top-tier science center.

It’s a good place to visit if you’re nearby or have a specific interest in science, but don’t expect to spend more than a few hours here. There’s potential for growth, and I hope they add more advanced exhibits and innovations in the future. Overall, worth a visit, but there’s room for improvement.

• Recommended for groups or science enthusiasts, but you may leave feeling like there's more that could be done.

Vasmasur Dada, often spelled as Bhasmasura, is a character from Hindu mythology. He was an asura (demon) who received a boon from Lord Shiva that allowed him to turn anyone he touched on the head into ashes (bhasma). The tale goes that Bhasmasura, intoxicated by his newfound power, attempted to use it on Lord Shiva himself. To escape, Shiva sought help from Lord Vishnu, who took the form of the enchanting Mohini. Mohini tricked Bhasmasura into touching his own head, thus turning himself to ashes. This story highlights themes of power, greed, and the eventual downfall of those who misuse their boons.

Bhalupahad, located in Syangja district, Nepal, is a picturesque region nestled amidst the breathtaking landscapes of the Himalayas. Characterized by its lush greenery, terraced fields, and traditional Nepalese architecture, Bhalupahad is a tranquil haven that captivates visitors with its natural beauty.

The village is surrounded by majestic mountains, providing a stunning backdrop to everyday life. The locals, predominantly engaged in agriculture, cultivate terraced fields that cascade down the hillsides, creating a mesmerizing patchwork of vibrant greenery. The agricultural practices are deeply rooted in the region's culture, and the terraces not only serve as a means of sustenance but also contribute to the area's scenic allure.

Bhalupahad is known for its warm and welcoming community, where traditions and customs are preserved with great pride. The village is home to various ethnic groups, each adding to the rich cultural tapestry of the region. Traditional festivals, dances, and rituals are integral to the community's social fabric, offering visitors a unique insight into the local way of life.

The surrounding natural environment provides ample opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts. Hiking trails meander through the hills, offering panoramic views of the Himalayan peaks and the lush valleys below. Bhalupahad also serves as a gateway to explore the diverse flora and fauna of the region, making it a destination not only for cultural enthusiasts but also for nature lovers.

In recent years, efforts have been made to promote sustainable tourism in Bhalupahad, aiming to preserve its pristine environment and promote responsible travel. As a result, visitors can experience the beauty of this Himalayan gem while contributing to the well-being of the local community and the preservation of its unique heritage. Bhalupahad stands as a testament to the harmonious coexistence of nature and culture in the heart of the Himalayas.

The Chhabdi Barahi Temple is located in Chhabdi Barahi Village, Tanahun District. It is the source of the Chhabdi River, which flows from a small pond in the temple compound. It is believed that Satyavati was born here in the form of a fish, and fishes play an important role in the cultural traditions of the temple. Death rites in keeping with Hindu traditions are performed for fishes that die here, with the priest playing the role of the son of the fish.

Along with that of Satyavati there are idols of many different gods and goddesses in the temple compound, including a temple of Bhimsen. Dozens of goats are sacrificed to Barahi every month. However, no animal sacrifice takes place during Aunsi, Ekadashi, and the month of Shrawan. It is also believed that menstruating women and their husbands should not visit the temple.

Chhabdi Barahi Temple (Mandir) is a holy temple situated in a hilly forest located in Tanahun district of western Nepal. It is said that Chhabdi Barahi and Dhor Barahi temples are sisters and both are religious temples according to Hindu mythology. The temple is dedicated to Fish Headed Goddess, which is known about two hundred years ago. Before the existence of the temple, the local people over there go fishing to this site and one day a fired arrow to fish mistakenly stuck in the rock and suddenly blood appears on it. After this incident, fishing was stopped to this site, instead, a small shrine was constructed to this site which is well known as Chhabdi Barahi Temple in these days.

Cholung Park: Explore Nature, Embrace Heritage!

Cholung Park, located in Terathum's Laligurans Municipality, is a hidden gem that beautifully blends cultural heritage with natural beauty. Known for its breathtaking views and vibrant rhododendron blooms, the park is especially popular during peak flowering season in March. It's an essential stop for anyone interested in the rich traditions of the indigenous Limbu community and offers an immersive experience into their history and spiritual beliefs.

The park's highlight is the mysterious "lung" stone pillars, thought to have been erected for rituals, grave markers, and to resolve clan disputes. These stones, alongside the sacred Cholung Worok Pond, embody the deep connection the Limbu people have with nature. Visitors can also explore ancient cultural artifacts, including sacred beads, weapons, and historical documents housed in the Yuma Museum.

Cholung Park also shines as a model for ecological conservation, with over 150 plant species, including medicinal herbs and various rhododendron species. The park provides a peaceful, educational experience with its traditional village square, nature trails, and cultural exhibits, all of which showcase the Limbu community's bond with their ancestors and environment.

If you're looking to learn about indigenous culture, explore stunning nature, or enjoy peaceful walks surrounded by breathtaking views, Cholung Park is a must-visit destination. Don't forget to capture the beautiful scenery for your photos!

Highlights:
- Stunning views with vibrant rhododendron blooms.
- Rich cultural and historical significance, showcasing Limbu traditions.
- The Yuma Museum with historical artifacts, including fossils and ancient documents.
- Sacred stone pillars ("lung") and a traditional Limbu village square.
- More than 150 species of plants, including medicinal herbs and rhododendron varieties.
- A peaceful spot for nature lovers and cultural enthusiasts alike.

Recommendations;
- Best time to visit: March for the rhododendron bloom.
- Ideal for photography, history buffs, and nature lovers.

Tenjure Dada in Basantpur offers a unique trekking experience with breathtaking sunrise and sunset views, showcasing the majestic Makalu massif and other Himalayan peaks. The trek, although requiring a 2-3 km walk, rewards with a display of thirty-four rhododendron varieties, making it the home to the most rhododendron species in Nepal. Known as the Rhododendron trail, it spans across Taplejung, Tehrathum, and Sankhuwasabha districts. You can get special drinks, local juice there, also local murga 😅

This hill, often considered a paradise on earth, is a haven for botanists exploring flower species. Spring is the ideal time to visit, allowing one to witness the vibrant blooms of rhododendrons. Additionally, the area hosts migrants from the northern Olangchung region, trans-Himalayan yak herders living on tsampa, dried yak meat, and cheese, adding a cultural touch to the natural beauty of Basantapur. Though the trek may challenge leg muscles, the scenic rewards make it a worthwhile journey.

Tute Deurali, located in Basantapur, Nepal, is a serene and picturesque destination that offers visitors a unique opportunity to experience the natural beauty and cultural richness of the Himalayan region. Situated amidst lush forests, rolling hills, and cascading waterfalls, Tute Deurali is a hidden gem that provides a tranquil retreat from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

The name "Tute Deurali" translates to "Broken Gate" in English, reflecting the rugged terrain and rocky landscape of the area. Despite its remote location, Tute Deurali is accessible via scenic trekking trails that wind through pristine forests and charming villages, offering visitors a chance to immerse themselves in the raw beauty of the Himalayas.

Tute Deurali is not only known for its natural beauty but also for its cultural significance. The area is home to several ancient temples, monasteries, and sacred sites, which are revered by the local communities. Visitors can explore these cultural landmarks, learn about the rich history and traditions of the region, and participate in religious ceremonies and rituals.

One of the highlights of visiting Tute Deurali is the opportunity to experience traditional Sherpa hospitality. Visitors can stay in cozy guesthouses or homestays run by local Sherpa families, who warmly welcome guests into their homes and provide them with delicious home-cooked meals and comfortable accommodations.

Tute Deurali also serves as a base camp for trekkers and adventurers looking to explore the surrounding Himalayan peaks. From here, visitors can embark on exhilarating treks to nearby mountains, including Taréba Him and other prominent peaks, offering stunning panoramic views of the Himalayan landscape.

Overall, Tute Deurali is a hidden paradise that captivates visitors with its natural beauty, cultural heritage, and warm hospitality. Whether seeking adventure, spiritual enlightenment, or simply a peaceful retreat in nature, travelers are sure to find solace and serenity in this enchanting destination nestled in the heart of Basantapur, Nepal.

The Patan Museum, located in the heart of Patan Durbar Square in Lalitpur, Nepal, is a treasure trove of traditional art and architecture. Housed within a meticulously restored palace, the museum is renowned for its vast collection of cultural artifacts, particularly those reflecting the rich history of the Kathmandu Valley. It was inaugurated in 1997 and has since become one of Nepal's most celebrated cultural landmarks.

The museum specializes in Hindu and Buddhist sculptures, showcasing works that span over 1,000 years. Many of the artifacts are crafted from bronze, stone, and wood, highlighting the exceptional craftsmanship of the Newar artisans. Among its prized exhibits are intricately carved statues of Hindu deities such as Vishnu, Shiva, and Durga, as well as Buddhist icons like Avalokiteshvara and Tara.

The architecture of the museum itself is a masterpiece. The building, a part of the former royal palace complex, blends traditional Newar design with modern restoration techniques. Its red brick facade, ornately carved wooden windows, and open courtyards reflect the grandeur of Nepal's Malla period. The museum's galleries are thoughtfully curated, offering detailed explanations about the historical, cultural, and religious significance of each artifact.

Beyond its exhibits, the museum provides visitors with insights into the philosophical and spiritual traditions of the region. Interactive displays and informative panels make it an engaging experience for both locals and international tourists.

The Patan Museum is not just a repository of artifacts; it is a celebration of Nepal's artistic heritage. With its serene ambiance and educational value, it offers a unique opportunity to delve into the history and spirituality of one of the world’s oldest cultures. A visit to the museum is an enriching experience that leaves visitors with a deeper appreciation for Nepal’s timeless artistry.

The International Mountain Museum (IMM) archives, documents, and displays the past and present of the mountaineering heritage. There are exhibits and artefacts on famous peaks, descriptions of famous mountaineers, the lifestyle of mountain people, flora and fauna, including geology, to represent the traditional culture and values of the Himalayan people. It also has a souvenir counter where you can buy the miniature of Mt. Everest. The IMM grounds have an artificial mountain that visitors may easily climb and photograph. Aside from that, you will be invited to enjoy a short film on the history of Himalaya. You'll also find million-year-old rocks and fossils there.

There is a restaurant near parking. Ticket price is 263 NPR. A fast walk across the museum will still require you 1-2 hours. It is wheelchair accessible. The museum itself is kept up nicely, but the restrooms could use some cleaning. No smoking on the perimeter.

The museum was inaugurated on 5 February 2004. More than 100,000 domestic and international tourists visit the International Mountain Museum (IMM) every year. IMM records, documents and exhibits the past and present developments related to mountain and mountaineering around the world.

The museum contains three main exhibition halls: Hall of Great Himalayas, Hall of Fame and Hall of World Mountains. There are exhibits on famous peaks, descriptions of famous mountaineers, the culture and lifestyle of mountain people, flora subscribe and fauna including geology, in an attempt to represent the traditional culture and values of the Nepalese people.

There is also an exhibition about the Yeti, an outdoors "living museum" dedicated to Nepal's indigenous tribes, and a 31-foot replica of Mt. Manaslu.

The museum runs under the direct supervision of Nepal's Department of Archeology.

Kathmandu Durbar Square, also known as Basantapur Durbar Square, is one of the three iconic Durbar Squares in the Kathmandu Valley and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Dating back to the 12th century, it served as the seat of power for the Malla and Shah kings. The square is a treasure trove of Newari architecture, featuring intricate wooden carvings, ancient temples, and cultural landmarks.

Key attractions include the Kumari Ghar (home of the living goddess), Kasthamandap, the historic Hanuman Dhoka Palace, and the Taleju Bhawani Temple, which opens only once a year on Navami during Dashain. Visitors can also admire the shrines of Lord Kaal Bhairav and Swet Bhairav.

Although some areas are still being restored after the 2015 earthquake, the preservation efforts are commendable, and the site's beauty remains intact. A local guide is highly recommended to fully appreciate the history and significance of this iconic landmark.

Tip: Visit early morning or late afternoon for fewer crowds and stunning light for photography.

The Patan Museum, located in the heart of Patan Durbar Square in Lalitpur, Nepal, is a treasure trove of traditional art and architecture. Housed within a meticulously restored palace, the museum is renowned for its vast collection of cultural artifacts, particularly those reflecting the rich history of the Kathmandu Valley. It was inaugurated in 1997 and has since become one of Nepal's most celebrated cultural landmarks.

The museum specializes in Hindu and Buddhist sculptures, showcasing works that span over 1,000 years. Many of the artifacts are crafted from bronze, stone, and wood, highlighting the exceptional craftsmanship of the Newar artisans. Among its prized exhibits are intricately carved statues of Hindu deities such as Vishnu, Shiva, and Durga, as well as Buddhist icons like Avalokiteshvara and Tara.

The architecture of the museum itself is a masterpiece. The building, a part of the former royal palace complex, blends traditional Newar design with modern restoration techniques. Its red brick facade, ornately carved wooden windows, and open courtyards reflect the grandeur of Nepal's Malla period. The museum's galleries are thoughtfully curated, offering detailed explanations about the historical, cultural, and religious significance of each artifact.

Beyond its exhibits, the museum provides visitors with insights into the philosophical and spiritual traditions of the region. Interactive displays and informative panels make it an engaging experience for both locals and international tourists.

The Patan Museum is not just a repository of artifacts; it is a celebration of Nepal's artistic heritage. With its serene ambiance and educational value, it offers a unique opportunity to delve into the history and spirituality of one of the world’s oldest cultures. A visit to the museum is an enriching experience that leaves visitors with a deeper appreciation for Nepal’s timeless artistry.

Muktinath Temple, a sacred site for both Hindus and Buddhists, is located in the Mustang district of Nepal at an altitude of 3,710 meters in the Himalayan range. Known as "Mukti Kshetra," meaning "place of liberation," it is a revered pilgrimage destination attracting devotees from Nepal, India, and beyond. The temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Hindu tradition and Avalokiteshvara in Buddhist belief, symbolizing a unique confluence of religious harmony.

The temple’s architecture is modest yet spiritually significant, with a pagoda-style structure surrounded by breathtaking landscapes of the Annapurna mountain range. A key feature of Muktinath is the 108 sacred water spouts shaped like bulls’ heads, known as "Muktidhara." Pilgrims bathe under these spouts, believing it cleanses them of sins. Adjacent to the temple is the eternal flame, or "Jwala Mai," fueled by natural gas, a phenomenon held sacred by both faiths.

Accessible via a challenging trek or helicopter ride, the journey to Muktinath is considered a part of the pilgrimage. The area is also rich in cultural significance, with monasteries, prayer wheels, and stone-carved deities adding to its spiritual aura. The nearby Kali Gandaki River is renowned for Shaligram stones, considered manifestations of Lord Vishnu. The temple operates year-round, though the peak season is from March to October.

The 31 species of mammals recorded include the Asian elephant, spotted deer, hog deer, wild boar, smooth-coated otter and golden jackal. The Ganges river dolphin has been sighted in the Koshi River. Gaur and nilgai have declined in numbers. Nepal’s last remaining population of about 150 wild water buffalo inhabit the area. This population has now grown to a total of 432 individuals with an annual growth rate of 7.27 percent, according to the latest census carried out in 2016. With this upsurge in the population, authorities are planning a possible transfer of some wild water buffaloes to the flood plains of Chitwan National Park where they have been extirpated around 1950's. If the proposed translocation happens, this will present a natural Predator-Prey scenario since wild water buffaloes in Koshi Tappu has been lacking their natural predators in the form of tiger, leopard and dhole for quite a long time.

The Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve is a protected area in the Terai of eastern Nepal covering 175 km2(68 sq mi) of wetlands in the Sunsari, Saptari and Udayapur Districts. It comprises extensive mudflats, reed beds, and freshwater marshes in the floodplain of the Sapta Kosi River, and ranges in altitude from 75 to 81 m (246 to 266 ft). It was established in 1976 and designated as a Ramsar site in December 1987.

A wide range of animals inhabit the protected area. In its water courses and ponds, 200 species of fish have been recorded, most of which are resident. Two toadspecies, nine frog species, six lizard species, five snake species and eleven turtle species are recorded Gharial and mugger crocodile occur as well.

Notable among the 485 bird species are watercock, Indian nightjar, dusky eagleowl, black-headed cuckooshrike, whitetailed stonechat, striated grassbird, large adjutant stork, Pallas’s fish eagle, common golden-eye, and gullbilled tern. Swamp francolinand rufous-vented grass babbler occur as well.
